simplified: Your dreams can give you new ideas about things you didn't know you were thinking about. Common dreams, like flying, falling, losing your teeth, or being naked in public, usually have similar meanings for many people. To understand what they mean for you, it's important to link them to your daily experiences and feelings.

One interesting example of wild animals in a city is the wild dogs of Moscow. About 35,000 wild dogs live on the streets of Moscow. Some were born wild, and others were pets that were left behind by their owners. Some dogs live alone, while others live in groups. In 2010, scientists studied these dogs and found that they have adapted very well to city life. They have learned it is safer to cross the street with people, and some dogs seem to understand traffic lights.

Wonder is RJ Palacio's first novel. She says on her website that she got the idea for the book after seeing a girl with facial differences on the street. Wonder has sold many copies in the United States and has won several awards. Many schools are using it to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. A movie is being made, and many people, including me, are excited to see what RJ Palacio will write next.

Chloe has two pet rats named Zena and Roxy. She knows they are not usual pets and has tried many times to tell people that rats are clean and can be great pets if cared for properly. She understands why some people don’t like them. She also didn’t like rats until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats, which were very loving and smart. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she wanted to keep two of them.

Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been hurt or killed in car accidents, and others have died from electric shocks while playing with wires. Baboons are an endangered species, so to protect them and reduce problems with people, the city council has hired a team of Baboon Monitors. Their job is to move baboons away from the city or catch them and release them in the countryside. This plan has worked somewhat, but it is difficult to keep baboons from returning to the city when they find easy food there.

I work for a global IT company, but since their main office is in the States, I do all my work online from home. This saves me time because I don’t have to travel or chat with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this flexibility is important to me because I can take time off when my children have school events or when I need to see the dentist. The downside is that without set office hours, I often work late into the evening and sometimes miss dinner to finish my work.

In the 1990s, graffiti kept going, but street art also grew a lot worldwide. Some artists wanted to share political messages and created art to make people think about war, inequality, and discrimination. Other street artists focused on making beautiful and appealing work. In South America, many street artists worked in poor neighborhoods, bringing color, life, and beauty to dull city walls.

Every day, social media, magazines, and store displays show people many things to buy, and British shoppers are purchasing more clothes and shoes than ever. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without much thought, and big brands sell cheap clothes that people often wear just a few times before throwing them away.

Sam squinted at the sun and saw the dust from the car going to the Big House. The horses were kicking and swatting flies, not caring that their owner was visiting after ten months. Sam waited. Mr. Carter only came out here when he needed to, which Sam liked. The more he stayed away from his boss, the longer he could keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped sweat from his neck. The wet spots on his shirt looked like shapes on a map. His skin was already getting red in the June sun. He looked like a man who made money while others did the work.

Many people in Berlin, Germany, said that shooting pigs was too cruel, and there were strong disagreements between hunters and animal lovers. In response to the protests, the city council chose to take a kinder approach to deal with the pigs. Instead of shooting them, they built fences and made it illegal to feed the pigs. We will see if this plan works, but it might be hard because warmer winters mean there are more pigs than before.

Suzanne was inspired to write the Hunger Games because she loves Greek mythology. As a child, she enjoyed the story of Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story, Athens is controlled by Crete, but the people of Athens fight back. As punishment, King Minos of Crete makes the Athenians send seven boys and seven girls to Crete each year. These young people are put into a maze and eaten by a monster called the Minotaur. However, one boy named Theseus fights and defeats the Minotaur. Suzanne sees Katniss Everdeen as a modern version of Theseus.

Zoos can teach people about protecting animals and their homes by bringing together people and animals. Some zoos help animals that were hurt in circuses or left behind as pets. They also do important research on how animals behave and how to help them when they are sick.

A new trend against consumerism is the 'buy nothing' trend. It started in Canada in the early 1990s and then spread to the US, where it opposes the excessive spending during Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On Buy Nothing Day, people protest and cut their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups help each other exchange and repair items they already have.

Is graffiti art or vandalism? It depends on how you see it, but in many places, writing or painting on public or private property is seen as vandalism. Many street artists have been stopped by the police, and some have had to pay fines. Many city councils say it costs a lot to clean graffiti off buildings, buses, and trains.

What do people in the art world think about graffiti and street art? Recently, more people have started to see it as valuable art. There have been big street art shows in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, American artist Elura Emerald put together a street art show in a New York gallery. She supported street artists by saying, "Artists who paint on the street are just expressing themselves and not hurting anyone. They should be valued and celebrated."

Most people have four to six dreams each night after they turn ten, which adds up to about 2,000 dreams a year. By the time someone is 80 years old, they might have had around 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 percent of our dreams, we still remember a few thousand throughout our lives. It’s easy to think that sometimes a dream can happen before something similar occurs in real life, especially if the dream is about something common in daily life.

The Hunger Games is set in the future, after North America was destroyed. The country is called Panem and has twelve poor districts ruled by the rich Capitol. The Capitol has complete control over the country. Each district makes different goods for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, supplies all the coal for Panem. There was a thirteenth district, but it rebelled against the Capitol and was destroyed.

Wild animals sometimes enter cities to find food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have begun to visit homes near the city to eat. They open trash bins and take fruit from gardens. Some bold baboons have even gone into people's houses to steal food from kitchens! Baboons can be dangerous and have hurt many pets, so many people in the city do not like having them around.

Many bridge accidents happen while the bridge is being built. These accidents often happen because the engineers make mistakes, like calculating wrong. The bridge can fall down because it is too heavy, which can be very dangerous for the workers on it.

George Lucas was one of the first film directors to use the 17 stages of the hero's journey in his stories. Usually, the hero begins with a normal life, but then something happens that leads them to an adventure that changes everything. In Star Wars, Luke has a normal life with his aunt and uncle, fixing robots. When he discovers Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi in the robot R2D2, it is the moment that starts his adventure.

One idea to stop an asteroid heading for Earth is to use a nuclear weapon to blow it up. This might seem like a movie story, like in the 1998 film Armageddon, but NASA has a real plan called the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER). They would shoot eight-ton rockets at the asteroid to try to change its path. If the asteroid is too close for this to work, the rockets would have nuclear bombs to destroy it.

Campbell says that the hero initially does not want to go on an adventure, but then a mentor helps them, and they choose to enter a special world where the adventure takes place. Next, the hero faces tests, fights enemies, and meets friends to get ready for their biggest challenge. For Luke, Obi-Wan is the mentor, Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO are the friends, and Darth Vader is the enemy in the special world of the Death Star.

Items that are not used much might seem worthless to some people, but they can be valuable to others. With the rise of the internet, online groups have found ways to make money by sharing these underused items. Using websites and social media groups that help buy and sell second-hand goods, it is now easier than ever for people to share with each other. This is called the sharing economy.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main ideas about dreams became popular. One idea was that dreams show things we don't know about ourselves. Freud thought that by understanding our dreams, we could learn about our hidden feelings and problems. The other idea was different; it said that dreams are just random brain activity while we organize memories from the day. When we wake up, we try to understand these random images and feelings and create a story from them.

I am a freelancer and work for myself. This is good because I can choose what I do and how I use my time. At first, I worked from home, but it was hard to focus because there were many distractions, like housework, tea, and family members needing my help. So, I started working at a café, but the Wi-Fi was not good and I drank too much coffee. Finally, I decided to rent a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers. I enjoyed getting dressed for work in the morning and being able to concentrate in an office.

NASA can find the remaining middle-sized NEOs if it gets money to build NEOCam, a 0.5-meter space telescope that uses infrared light to find asteroids. If it gets the money, it could reach its goal in ten years. After that, the planetary defense team would still need to figure out how to protect the planet from the really dangerous asteroids – the PHAs.

The 'buy nothing' trend has reached social media influencers who usually post about clothes and make-up to buy. Some YouTube stars now tell their viewers not to buy anything for up to a year. Two friends in Canada spent a year only buying food. In the first three months, they learned to live without buying electronics, clothes, or home items. In the next stage, they stopped using services like haircuts, eating at restaurants, or buying gas for their cars. In one year, they saved $55,000.

Pi cares about religion. His family is Hindu, but he is interested in other religions and becomes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. To everyone's surprise, Pi says he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. When his family and teachers ask him to pick one religion, Pi says, "I just want to love God." After that, his family and teachers let him choose his own beliefs about religion.

Some people believe that writing down your dreams can help you have lucid dreams. Lucid dreams are when you know you are dreaming and can control what happens in the dream. This means you could change a scary dream into a nice one or guide the story of your dream like a movie director. Instead of just figuring out what your dreams mean, you will be making them, but you might still want some dreams that let your mind share its thoughts!

Many people do not know they contribute to the disposable clothing issue because they give their old clothes to charities. However, charity shops cannot sell all these clothes. 'Fast fashion' quickly goes out of style and is often too low quality to recycle; people do not want to buy it used. A lot of it gets thrown away, and many clothes that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries, creating more economic and environmental problems.

Some adventurers, like Meagan McGrath from Canada, take on many challenges. She has climbed the highest mountains, biked across Canada, and run a long race in the Sahara Desert. Her most amazing trip was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and needed help. Many people would have stopped there, but Meagan kept going. After forty days, she reached the South Pole, pulling a sled with her tent and food through very cold weather and ice storms.

Blek le Rat began by painting rats on the walls in Paris. Now, he wants people to think about social issues. He paints pictures of homeless people in big cities to make residents think about homelessness.

In some places, local governments have tried to help artists by giving them special areas to paint instead of letting them paint graffiti anywhere. Taiwan has 'graffiti zones' where artists can paint on walls. In São Paulo, Brazil, the city has even let some graffiti artists paint on subway trains.

Faith47 is from Cape Town, South Africa. She paints large, colorful pictures of people and animals and enjoys visiting different places. You can see her art on sidewalks, in empty factories, and on old cars. She appreciates that most street art does not last long and will be washed away by rain or cleaned up by city workers. To her, this shows that life is always changing with its endings and new starts.

Gabriela's old workplace had a culture where leaders were respected and made decisions without being questioned, while her Swedish team was used to a culture where everyone, including bosses, worked together to solve problems and make decisions.

When Gabriela noticed the cultural differences between her and her team, she decided to talk openly with them about how they felt about her leadership. Her team was happy to share their thoughts and said they were not used to being told what to do. They liked having more freedom to take initiative and be creative. When Gabriela told them exactly what to do, they felt she did not trust them to do their jobs well. They understood that Gabriela took it personally when they tried to suggest changes to her decisions, and they explained that this was how they had always worked.

Os Gêmeos are identical twin brothers from São Paulo. They paint many things, from small tags to large, colorful pictures of people on buildings. Their art is often very big, so they use cranes to help them. In 2007, they painted an entire castle in Scotland.

Throughout history, people have painted and written on walls. In prehistoric times, people in Africa and Europe painted pictures of animals and people in caves. Graffiti has been discovered on buildings in ancient places like Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists found many examples of graffiti written in Latin, including religious, political, and romantic messages, as well as some magic spells!

Have you ever wanted to climb Mount Everest or walk to the South Pole? If yes, you are not the only one. Every year, many people try to climb the highest mountains or walk across continents. Unlike explorers in the past who used maps and compasses, today’s adventurers use modern tools like GPS and satellite phones. Many of these adventurers love nature and travel to raise awareness about environmental problems, while others want to help people in need and raise money for charities.

The first test is called DART, which stands for the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. They plan to test DART on a moon of an asteroid named Didymos. This moon, called 'Didymoon,' is 150 meters wide and goes around its larger asteroid, which is 800 meters wide. They hope that when DART hits it, it will change its path enough for telescopes on Earth to see.

The main character of the story is a sixteen-year-old girl named Katniss Everdeen. She lost her father in a mining accident and must find food for her family. She hunts in the woods near District 12 with her friend Gale and becomes very good at using a bow and arrow. When her younger sister, Prim, is picked as a tribute, Katniss decides to go in her place. The other tribute from District 12 is a boy named Peeta, and Katniss soon has a complicated relationship with him.

Writing about your dreams will help you remember more details, so think about the people and places in your dreams because they might be important too. After a week, you will be surprised by how much you have written. Now you can link your dreams to what happens and how you feel in your daily life.

In the past, many bridges were built from wood and were very easy to catch fire. This was especially true for old train bridges, where sparks from steel wheels on steel tracks could sometimes set a bridge on fire and make it burn down.

We cannot predict how street art will change in the future, but we see some trends. Most street artists are young and paint in their local areas, but many are now traveling and working worldwide. Some artists use the internet to communicate and share pictures of their art. The art world is also starting to recognize street art as real art. Even though we don't know what will happen next, we can be sure that street art is not going away!

Suzanne Collines has always felt sad when watching news about wars. When she was a child, her father was a pilot in the US Air Force and fought in Vietnam. Her mother tried to keep her safe by not talking about the war, but she still saw news about it and knew her dad was there. It was very scary for her.

A global survey by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) gathered responses from over 40,000 millennials (born between 1983 and 1993) and non-millennials about workplace culture, communication, pay, career growth, and work-life balance. Another survey by Deloitte included over 10,000 millennials who shared their views on the challenges and chances in today's work environment.

Erik Weihenmayer from the United States is an adventurer. He has ridden a bike in the deserts of Morocco, kayaked in the Grand Canyon, and climbed Mount Everest. Remarkably, Erik has been blind since he was 13 years old. Besides his travels, he helps people with disabilities to be active and takes groups of young blind people climbing.

Online platforms are giving people a chance to earn some extra money. For example, busy parents used to avoid selling their children's old items at local markets, but now they can easily sell barely used baby clothes and expensive baby gear online to make some cash.

Pi and Richard Parker are in the lifeboat for 227 days. They face hunger, sickness, and tiredness. They go through strong storms and the hot sun of the Pacific, but they manage to survive. Sometimes, Pi feels comfort from his three religions, but other times he feels very lonely and sad. At last, they see the Mexican coast, and everything changes. I won't tell you the ending, so you need to read the book to see what happens to Pi and Richard Parker when they see land.

Chloe came home from school, made a cup of coffee, and took it to her bedroom. She had homework to do, but that could wait. She wanted to enjoy the quiet time before her parents got home and the house became noisy with talking, the TV, or her dad listening to jazz while cooking. She liked this time because she could play with her pet rats.

In 2010, NASA's planetary defense team found and recorded 90 percent of the asteroids near Earth that are 1 kilometer wide. These 'near-Earth objects' (NEOs) are as big as mountains and include anything within 50 million kilometers of Earth's orbit. NASA estimates there are about 50 more to record, but says none of the 887 known NEOs are a serious threat to the planet.

Auggie decides to go to school, but his first day is very hard because he feels anxious and different. Other kids don't want to sit with him and often stare or whisper about him. Luckily, he makes friends with Jack and Summer. However, Auggie finds out that some classmates are afraid to touch him. Throughout the school year, he experiences many highs and lows until a surprising and difficult event at a school camp changes everything.

The two men looked at the northern part of the land, which seemed to go on forever. They could barely see the fences from where they were. No matter how bored or rebellious a teenage boy might feel, he couldn't escape on foot. Sam watched the biggest horse, which was kicking the ground with its strong hooves. He wondered if the boy could ride. A good rider could find a lot of trouble out here, far from anyone else. But someone who didn't know about horses and wanted to run away from his father might find even more trouble.

More than 4,000 climbers, aged thirteen to eighty, have reached the top of Everest. Climbing high mountains in cold weather and strong storms is still very dangerous, but the best climbers in the world now seek new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria started loving mountain climbing when she was a teenager. After finishing school, she worked as a nurse but continued to climb in her free time.

After climbing Everest, Gerlinde chose to climb all fourteen of the world's mountains that are 8,000 meters high. To make it harder, she climbs without oxygen tanks, which is dangerous because low oxygen at high altitudes can harm the brain and body. Gerlinde also uses her fame as a climber to help a charity for poor children and orphans in Nepal.

If we look at the things we have bought in our lives, we will see that not everything is used well: the warm coat we thought was stylish even though we live in a hot country, the smartphone we stopped using when we got a new one, the car we only drive on weekends, or the guest room that has become a storage room.

Throughout history and in different cultures, dreams have been linked to prophecy. People believed that dreams were messages from the gods, meant to give us knowledge or understanding. Even now, many people remember a time when they dreamed about something, and later that dream happened in real life.

Many large and costly transportation projects around the world include building bridges. Bridges are important connections that allow cars, trucks, and trains to cross water, deep valleys, or other roads. Therefore, they are a key part of civil engineering and are closely examined, especially if they fall down.

After weeks of frustration, Gabriela emailed her Swedish manager about the problems she had with her team. Her manager just asked if she thought her team was still doing well and what could help her work better with them. Gabriela thought her manager was unclear and didn’t feel he was handling the situation well.

Dogs that live in groups have learned that humans often give food to smaller, cuter dogs, so those dogs go to ask for food for everyone. Some dogs have even figured out how to use the metro to move around their area! Scientists are not sure how the dogs know when to get off the train. One idea is that they use their strong sense of smell to recognize the scents of places they like. Another idea is that they understand the names of stations from the announcements. Either way, people on the metro are now so used to seeing dogs on the trains that they hardly notice them.

Ed Stafford from the UK was the first person to walk the whole length of the Amazon River. He began at a small stream in the Andes mountains of Peru and reached the river's end in Brazil after two years and four months, walking 6,000 kilometers. The Amazon rainforest has dangerous animals like poisonous snakes, crocodiles, and jaguars, so Ed was always at risk. Fortunately, he only got a few thousand bites from mosquitoes and ants.

In Britain, the average person spends over £1,000 on new clothes each year, which is about four percent of their income. This may not seem like a lot, but it shows two bigger problems for society and the environment. First, many people are using credit cards to pay for these clothes. Right now, British adults owe about £670 each to credit card companies, which is 66 percent of what they spend on clothes. Also, people are spending money they don’t have to buy things they don’t need. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothing every year, most of which ends up in landfills.

Ed's walk would not have been possible without technology. He used a radio to ask the rainforest people for food and permission to cross their land. Many of them came to meet him and helped him through the hardest parts of the journey. As he walked, Ed wrote a blog about his daily experiences. He used the media attention from his trip to speak out against the destruction of the rainforest and to raise money for environmental and children's charities in Brazil and Peru.

Businesses have realized that they can make money from the sharing economy by using resources that are not fully used. A popular business model now is for companies to create online platforms that connect customers with people who offer specific products or services. For example, Airbnb helps people rent out their empty rooms and houses for extra income. Another example is Uber, which allows people to use their own cars as taxis to earn extra money in their spare time.

One important job of modern zoos is to help with breeding programs for endangered animals. In nature, some rare animals struggle to find partners and have babies, and they face dangers from poachers, losing their homes, and predators. A good zoo allows these animals to live and breed safely. Also, as some wild animal numbers decrease, there is a risk that their genes become too similar. Breeding programs help by allowing zoo-bred animals to be released into the wild, which increases genetic diversity.

Both types of accidents are very rare, but boats and trains can make a bridge fall for different reasons. Trains can cause a bridge to fall because of their speed. Boats can cause a bridge to fall because they are very heavy, even if they are moving slowly. The best way to prevent bridge failures is to prepare for them. New technologies that find weak spots, safer work areas, and better designs can help reduce these serious accidents.

At first, Pi is scared of the animals and jumps into the ocean. Then he remembers there are hungry sharks in the water and knows he must climb back into the lifeboat. One by one, the animals in the lifeboat kill and eat each other until only Pi and the tiger are left. Luckily for Pi, the tiger, whom he names Richard Parker, feels sick and does not want to eat him right away.

When Pi is 16, a new government is chosen that his parents do not like. Worried about what will happen next, Pi's parents decide to close the zoo and move to Canada. Some animals are sold to zoos in North America, and the family travels by ship to Canada with the animals. During the journey, a big storm happens and the ship sinks. Sadly, Pi's family and the sailors drown, but Pi ends up in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orangutan, and a large tiger.

The Hunger Games is a very popular book for teens and young adults by American author Suzanne Collins. Since it came out in 2008, it has been translated into 26 languages and has sold millions of copies worldwide. It was also the first book for young readers to sell over a million e-books. The Hunger Games is now a big Hollywood movie and is just as successful, making 152.5 million dollars in its opening weekend in North America!

Dreams might happen because our mind is sorting out our daily thoughts, but they show up in dreams with special meanings. When we are awake, we usually think in words, like talking to ourselves. However, when we sleep, the part of our brain for language is less active, while the part for emotions is more active.

Having good relationships is very important for happiness. A study showed that happy people usually have strong connections with friends and family and spend time with them often. You also need at least one person to share your personal feelings with, which is called 'self-disclosure'. Just one close friend for deep conversations is enough, along with other relationships. It's not enough to have many friends just to hang out with or talk about music or football. That deeper connection is very important. Some people need to learn how to listen well to others to build stronger relationships.

Psychologist Carol Dweck talked about how our brains can change and how we can learn new skills, even if we weren't good at them before. Many people often praise the final results and natural talents, like saying, "You are great at noticing details" or "You are really good at planning events." However, studies show that if we focus on how things are done—by praising effort, trying new things, and solving problems—we can help people learn new skills and improve their talents.

The rover checks the air around it from time to time, and in 2014 it discovered that the air had methane, which is a simple organic molecule and an important part of natural gas. Methane only lasts for a few hundred years, so something on Mars must be making more of it. NASA says Mars releases thousands of tons of methane at once. The amount of methane goes up and down with the seasons, like the planet is breathing.

When she was starting her career, psychologist Carol Dweck from Stanford University gave ten-year-olds some problems that were a bit too difficult. One group liked the challenge and believed they could get better at it. She called this a 'growth mindset' because they thought about what they could achieve later. However, another group felt judged and thought they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and couldn't see how they could improve. Some of these children said they might cheat later, while others tried to find someone who did worse than them to feel better about themselves.

Horror films often take place in empty locations like abandoned hospitals, scary houses, or ghost towns. These lonely places make us wonder what life was like when people were there and why they left. Their silence can be very frightening too. Plus, these places are useful for horror film directors because there is usually no phone signal there.

Basements are always scary in horror films, no matter what type of house it is. They are often dark and damp, and you can only get to them by a narrow staircase. Something usually hides there, or the bad person keeps their tools there. Basements feel creepy, even if there is nothing in them.

Gary Collins, a policeman not on duty, was watching the London riots on TV. He quickly recognized some people and shortened his holiday to help identify them. He spent six months reviewing the CCTV footage and identified 190 people, often just by their eyes. His help was very important for the investigation. Even with 200,000 hours of video, facial recognition software only identified one person.

I find it interesting to think about how we can make our evolution faster by improving our bodies. Imagine if we could put a computer in our brain! Soon, we will be able to do this and improve our math skills, how we see and hear, and our memory. This idea will become more common.

The talk was interesting, and the speaker made some good points. For example, how can we expect teenagers not to text while doing homework when they see their parents using social media while cooking or waiting at a red light? She also pointed out that people want to be in many places at once, so they switch between real-life and online conversations. I notice this with my teenage daughter and her friends; they meet up but often sit quietly while talking to others online.

While news stories may make us think the world is getting more violent, there is some good news too. From the end of World War II to 1990, there were 30 wars that killed over 100,000 people. Today, there are still civil wars, but countries are generally living together more peacefully than before. However, terrorism has increased in recent years, and since World War II, more civilians have died in wars than soldiers. Still, the statistics for civilians are not all bad. Although violent crime is nine times more likely to cause deaths than political conflict, the global murder rate has slightly decreased, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

Wasfia has spent her life helping human rights and has seen many projects in her country that teach women and girls, but often these projects end and leave them with nothing. She realized that Bangladesh needed to be strong, so she combined her love for climbing and human rights to change how people think about women in her country. She started climbing while working on humanitarian projects in Tibet and Nepal because most people in flat Bangladesh have never seen a mountain. Her campaign is working, as people in her country and around the world are starting to pay attention.

Many people think that developing countries are very poor, ruled by dictators, and have no chance for improvement. However, this is not true. In fact, a big change is happening. In the last 20 years, over 700 million people have earned more money and escaped poverty. Also, six million fewer children die from sickness each year, more girls are going to school, and many more people have clean water.

Many managers try to make their feedback more positive by placing negative comments between two positive ones. However, if this becomes a habit, employees may see positive feedback as just a way to soften the negatives, which makes it less valuable. Positive feedback should not just be used to soften the negative but should be given to support and encourage good performance.

I am part of the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Forget the scary movie image of a Terminator stepping on human skulls and think about what is happening now: military machines like drones and robots are already being used to kill with little human control. The next step will be robots that can decide who to kill by themselves. I believe this would be very wrong and dangerous for people. We must be very careful about what we let machines do.

More people are learning English than all other languages together, and English is spoken in the most countries. However, Chinese has the most native speakers. There is not much connection between the number of native speakers and learners, but there is a stronger connection between the number of learners and the number of countries where the language is spoken.

Your manager stops you and says she wants to talk about how you did on the recent project. You worry about it all weekend, thinking about what you might have done wrong. When you go into her office on Monday morning, she starts by complimenting your good work on the project, and you wonder if this is just the usual nice comment before the real feedback. You know the feedback sandwich: say something nice, give the real feedback, and then say something nice again.

Born in the USA is a lively rock album with catchy songs, but its lyrics are deep and emotional. The songs tell stories about the struggles of everyday people who feel angry and disappointed because life hasn’t given them wealth or fame. For example, the song Glory Days is about small-town people remembering their youth, while Downbound Train is about a young man whose life falls apart after losing his job. It seems the artist is inspired by real people he knew and what his life could have been if he hadn’t become famous. The album clearly shows the amazing talent of the Boss.

Lewis wants the number of marine protected areas in the world to grow from 3 percent to 10 percent to help fix the harm done by human activities like overfishing, pollution, and littering. He has seen this damage himself during his trips. He has swum over coral reefs that have lost their color because the water is too warm and has seen lifeless areas in the shallow Red Sea filled with plastic. Pugh thinks that nature can heal if it has enough space, but time is running out. If we don't take care of our oceans, we might face a big problem soon.

Terrie Sharp, a best-selling author who has won the Olive Crime Writer Award twice, knows how to tell great stories. She grew up in a tough area of Glasgow and learned to stay safe and open car doors with a knife. Fortunately, she only uses her skills for writing her books, and now she is more talkative, appearing on popular daytime shows like Police Today and at writing conferences across the UK.

Is life getting worse every day? Is it impossible to make progress? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker examines human progress and finds positive news. We are living longer, healthier, freer, and happier lives. Pinker believes the real issue is that the values of reason and science from the Enlightenment are being challenged. When people in the media and leaders play on our tribal feelings, hopelessness, and distrust, we risk harming important things like democracy and global cooperation.

In old horror movies, when the main characters were in trouble, they often couldn't call for help or the police. Now, with mobile phones, that seems less real. To keep the suspense, there is no phone signal! If you are a hero in a horror movie, it's likely that when you really need to call for help, you won't have any signal. Or your phone battery will die right when you try to call. Or both.

In the 1950s, banana farmers in Central America were losing their most profitable banana, the Gros Michel, also called Big Mike. Now, the same problem is happening to its replacement, the Cavendish. The Gros Michel banana was popular because it was easy to transport, had a thick skin, and tasted sweet. United Fruit, the biggest banana grower and exporter in South America at that time, produced bananas very efficiently by cloning shoots from the plants instead of using seeds and growing them in crowded fields.

Most spiders have venom that helps them catch their food, not to hurt people. Only 25 types of spiders can harm humans, and while their bites can hurt, they usually are not deadly. The Sydney funnel-web spider in Australia has not killed anyone since the anti-venom was made in 1981. However, be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas. If they feel threatened, they can release irritating hairs that can get stuck in your skin or eyes.

This common idea in horror films was very popular in the late 20th century. It begins with a group of teenagers having fun, and it ends with everyone dead except one girl. At first, the girl is usually innocent, shy, and not very strong. By the end, she becomes the strongest and smartest person. The last girl almost always wins in the end.

To understand where our ability to use complex language comes from, we need to examine how our brains are different from those of other animals. This is not just about brain size; it also matters what other functions our brains have and how and why they developed over time. There are very few physical clues to help us; the tools left by our ancestors do not show us what kind of speech they could produce. However, we can see changes in the mouth, throat, and tongue of early humans. By around 100,000 years ago, humans could make complex sounds, but before that, scientists can only guess if early humans used simpler sounds to communicate.

Society, not nature, tells us that girls should prefer arts and humanities while boys take maths and physics. There are also not enough positive female role models in science jobs for young people to see. Cartoons and stories often show male scientists, inventors, or astronauts. Additionally, there is a wrong idea that scientists are nerdy, have bad social skills, or work alone and away from others. These false stereotypes from the media may make girls feel they do not belong in science and see it as an unattractive career. If girls had more positive female role models in science, it would help them feel more confident and included in those subjects.

The Scallion is a free weekly newspaper made by students and given out in faculty buildings, read by about 10,000 students. A survey shows that university students and staff appreciate it for entertainment, culture, and work experience. Printing the newspaper costs a lot. Some students find it hard to get a copy because they must go to the university to pick it up. Also, many copies become litter on campus.

At Girox Foods, about 12 out of every 100 employees leave each year. This number seems high because the usual rate in the industry is 7 out of 100. This report aims to find out why employees feel engaged at work and to suggest ways to make their experience better and keep them from leaving.

Much of what the speaker said was true. I believe that being more connected can make us feel more alone. My generation, who grew up without technology, knows how to be alone and that it's okay. But for those under 20, it's different. They are so busy talking online that they don't know how to enjoy being alone. Also, they learn to talk through messages that can be changed, instead of learning how to have real conversations face to face.

Don't always give negative feedback after positive feedback. If you always mix them, people might not value the positive comments. Make sure to give positive feedback sometimes without adding criticism.

Your dreams can give you new ideas about things you didn't know you were thinking about. Common dreams, like flying, falling, losing teeth, or being naked in public, usually have similar meanings for many people. To understand what they mean for you, think about how they relate to your daily life and feelings.

One interesting example of wild animals in a city is the wild dogs of Moscow. About 35,000 wild dogs live on the streets of Moscow. Some were born wild, and others were pets that people left behind. Some dogs live by themselves, while others live in groups. In 2010, scientists studied these dogs and found that they have adapted very well to city life. They have learned it is safer to cross the street with people, and some dogs seem to understand traffic lights.

Wonder is RJ Palacio's first novel. She says on her website that she got the idea for the book after seeing a girl with facial differences on the street. Wonder has sold many copies in the United States and has won several awards. Many schools are using it to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. A movie is being made, and many people, including me, are excited to see what RJ Palacio will write next.

Chloe has two pet rats named Zena and Roxy. She knows they are not usual pets and has tried many times to tell people that rats are clean and can be great pets if cared for properly. She understands why some people don’t like them. She also didn’t like rats until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats, which were very loving and smart. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she wanted to keep two of them.

Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been hurt or killed in car accidents, and others have died from electric shocks while playing with wires. Baboons are an endangered species, so to protect them and reduce problems with people, the city council has hired a team of Baboon Monitors. Their job is to move baboons away from the city or catch them and release them in the countryside. This plan has worked somewhat, but it is difficult to keep baboons from returning to the city when they find easy food there.

I work for a global IT company, but since their main office is in the States, I do all my work online from home. This means I don't waste time commuting or chatting with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this flexibility is important to me because I can take time off when my children have school events or when I need to go to the dentist. The downside is that without set office hours, I often work late into the evening and sometimes skip dinner to finish my work.

In the 1990s, graffiti kept going, but street art also grew a lot around the world. Some artists wanted to share political messages and created art to make people think about war, inequality, and discrimination. Other street artists focused on making beautiful and appealing work. In South America, many street artists worked in poor neighborhoods, bringing color, life, and beauty to dull city walls.

Every day, social media, magazines, and store displays show people many things to buy, and British shoppers are purchasing more clothes and shoes than ever. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without much thought, and big brands sell cheap clothes that people often wear just a few times before throwing them away.

Sam squinted at the sun and saw a dust trail from the car going to the Big House. The horses kicked at flies and didn't care that their owner was visiting after ten months. Sam waited because Mr. Carter only came out when necessary, which Sam liked. The more he stayed away from his boss, the longer he could keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped sweat from his neck, and the wet spots on his shirt looked like shapes on a map. His skin was getting red in the June sun, and he had the tan of a man who made money while others worked.

Many people in Berlin, Germany, said that shooting pigs was too cruel, and there were strong disagreements between hunters and animal lovers. In response to the protests, the city council chose to take a kinder approach to deal with the pigs. Instead of shooting them, they built fences and made it illegal to feed the pigs. We will see if this plan works, but it might be hard because warmer winters mean there are more pigs than before.

Suzanne was inspired to write the Hunger Games because she loves Greek mythology. As a child, she enjoyed the story of Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story, Athens is controlled by Crete, but the people of Athens fight back. As a punishment, King Minos of Crete makes the Athenians send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. These young people are put into a maze and eaten by a monster called the Minotaur. However, one boy named Theseus fights and kills the Minotaur. Suzanne thinks of Katniss Everdeen as a modern version of Theseus.

Zoos can teach people about protecting animals and their homes by bringing together people and animals. Some zoos help animals that were hurt in circuses or left behind as pets. They also do important research on how animals behave and how to help them when they are sick.

A new trend is growing against consumerism called the 'buy nothing' trend. It started in Canada in the early 1990s and then spread to the US, where it opposes the excessive spending during Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On Buy Nothing Day, people hold protests and cut their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups help people exchange and repair items they already have.

Is graffiti art or vandalism? It depends on how you see it, but in many places, writing or painting on public or private property is seen as vandalism. Many street artists have been stopped by the police, and some have had to pay fines. Many city councils say it costs a lot to clean graffiti off buildings, buses, and trains.

What do people in the art world think about graffiti and street art? Recently, more people have started to see it as valuable art. There have been big street art shows in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, American artist Elura Emerald held a street art show in a New York gallery. She supported street artists, saying, "Artists who paint on the street are just expressing themselves and not hurting anyone. They should be valued and celebrated."

Most people have four to six dreams each night after they turn ten, which adds up to about 2,000 dreams a year. By the time they are 80, an average person may have had around 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 percent of our dreams, we still remember a few thousand throughout our lives. It’s easy to think that a dream might match something that happens in real life, especially if the dream is about something common.

The Hunger Games is set in the future, after North America was destroyed. The country is called Panem and has twelve poor districts ruled by the rich Capitol. The Capitol has complete control over the country. Each district makes different goods for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, supplies all the coal for Panem. There was a thirteenth district, but it rebelled against the Capitol and was destroyed.

Wild animals sometimes enter cities to find food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have begun to visit homes near the city to eat. They open trash bins and take fruit from gardens. Some bold baboons have even gone into people's houses to steal food from kitchens! Baboons can be dangerous and have hurt many pets, so many people in the city do not like having them around.

Many bridge accidents happen while the bridge is being built. These accidents often happen because the engineers make mistakes, like calculating wrong. The bridge can fall down because it is too heavy, which can be very dangerous for the workers on it.

George Lucas was one of the first film directors to use the 17 stages of the hero's journey in his stories. Usually, the hero begins with a normal life, but then something happens that leads them to an adventure that changes everything. In Star Wars, Luke has a normal life with his aunt and uncle, fixing robots. When he discovers Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi in the robot R2D2, it is the moment that starts his adventure.

One idea to stop an asteroid heading for Earth is to use a nuclear weapon to blow it up. This might seem like a movie story, like in the 1998 film Armageddon, but NASA has a real plan called the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER). They would shoot eight-ton rockets at the asteroid to try to change its path. If the asteroid is too close for this to work, the rockets would have nuclear bombs to destroy it.

Campbell says that the hero initially does not want to go on an adventure, but then a mentor helps them, and they choose to enter a special world where the adventure takes place. Next, the hero faces tests, fights enemies, and meets friends to get ready for their biggest challenge. For Luke, Obi-Wan is the mentor, Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO are the friends, and Darth Vader is the enemy in the special world of the Death Star.

Items that are not used much might seem useless to some people, but they can be valuable to others. With the rise of the internet, online groups have found ways to make money by sharing these underused items. Using websites and social media groups to buy and sell second-hand goods, it is now easier than ever for people to share with each other. This is called the sharing economy.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main ideas about dreams became popular. One idea was that dreams show things we do not know about ourselves. Freud thought that by understanding our dreams, we could learn about our hidden feelings and the problems they cause. The other idea was different; it said that dreams are just random brain activity while we organize memories from the day. When we wake up, we try to understand these random images and feelings and create a story from them.

I am a freelancer and work for myself, which is great because I can choose what I do and how I use my time. At first, I worked from home, but it was hard to focus because there were too many distractions, like housework, tea, and family members needing my help. So, I started working at a café, but the Wi-Fi was not good, and I drank too much coffee. Finally, I decided to rent a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers. I enjoyed getting dressed for work in the morning and being able to concentrate in an office.

NASA's ability to find the remaining middle-sized NEOs depends on getting funding to build NEOCam, a 0.5-meter space telescope that uses infrared light to find asteroids. If they receive the funding, they could likely reach their goal in ten years. After that, the planetary defense team would still need to figure out how to protect the planet from the most concerning asteroids – the PHAs.

The 'buy nothing' trend has reached social media influencers who usually post about clothes and make-up to buy. Some YouTube stars now tell their viewers not to buy anything for up to a year. Two friends in Canada spent a year only buying food. For the first three months, they learned to live without buying electronics, clothes, or home items. In the next stage, they stopped using services like haircuts, eating at restaurants, or buying gas for their cars. In one year, they saved $55,000.

Pi cares about religion. His family is Hindu, but he is interested in other religions and becomes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. To everyone's surprise, Pi says he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. When his family and teachers ask him to pick one religion, Pi says, "I just want to love God." After that, his family and teachers let him choose his own beliefs about religion.

Some people believe that writing down your dreams can help you have lucid dreams. Lucid dreams are when you know you are dreaming and can change what happens in the dream. This means you could change a scary dream into a nice one or control the story of your dream like a movie director. Instead of just understanding your dreams, you will be making them, but you might still want some dreams that let your mind share what it is thinking!

Many people do not know they contribute to the problem of disposable clothing because they give their old clothes to charities. However, charity shops cannot sell all these clothes. 'Fast fashion' quickly goes out of style and is often too low quality to recycle; people do not want to buy it used. A lot of it gets thrown away, and many clothes that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries, creating more economic and environmental issues.

Some adventurers, like Meagan McGrath from Canada, take on many challenges. She has climbed the highest mountains, biked across Canada, and run a long race in the Sahara Desert. Her most amazing trip was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and needed help. Many people would have stopped there, but Meagan kept going. After forty days, she reached the South Pole, pulling a sled with her tent and food through very cold weather and ice storms.

Blek le Rat began by painting rats on the walls in Paris. Now, he wants people to think about social issues. He paints pictures of homeless people in big cities to make residents think about homelessness.

In some places, local governments have tried to help artists by giving them special areas to paint instead of letting them paint graffiti anywhere. Taiwan has 'graffiti zones' where artists can paint freely. In São Paulo, Brazil, the city has even let some graffiti artists paint on subway trains.

Faith47 is from Cape Town, South Africa. She paints large, colorful pictures of people and animals and enjoys visiting different places. You can see her art on sidewalks, in empty factories, and on old cars. She likes that most street art does not last long and will be washed away by rain or cleaned up by city workers. To her, this shows that life is always changing with its endings and new starts.

Gabriela's old workplace had a culture where people respected power and authority, and leaders made most decisions without being questioned. In contrast, her Swedish team was used to a culture where everyone, including bosses and workers, worked together to solve problems and make decisions, with leaders acting as coaches who welcome new ideas and challenges.

When Gabriela noticed the cultural differences with her team, she decided to talk openly with them about how they felt about her leadership. Her team was happy to share their thoughts and said they were not used to being told what to do. They liked having more freedom to take initiative and be creative. When Gabriela told them exactly what to do, they felt she didn't trust them to do their jobs well. They understood that Gabriela took it personally when they tried to suggest changes to her decisions and explained that this was how they had always worked.

Os Gêmeos are identical twin brothers from São Paulo. They paint many things, including big, colorful pictures of people on buildings. Their art is so large that they need cranes to help them. In 2007, they painted an entire castle in Scotland.

Throughout history, people have painted and written on walls. In prehistoric times, people in Africa and Europe painted pictures of animals and people in caves. Graffiti has been discovered on buildings in ancient places like Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists found many examples of graffiti written in Latin, including messages about religion, politics, love, and even some magic spells!

Have you ever wanted to climb Mount Everest or walk to the South Pole? If yes, you are not the only one. Every year, many people try to climb the highest mountains or walk across countries. Unlike explorers in the past who used maps and compasses, today’s adventurers use modern tools like GPS and satellite phones. Many of them love nature and travel to raise awareness about environmental problems, while others want to help people in need and collect money for charities.

The first is DART, which stands for the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. There are plans to test DART on the moon of an asteroid named Didymos. 'Didymoon' is 150 meters wide and goes around its bigger asteroid, which is 800 meters wide. We hope that when DART hits it, it will change its path enough for telescopes on Earth to see.

The main character of the story is a sixteen-year-old girl named Katniss Everdeen. She lost her father in a mining accident and must find food for her family. Katniss hunts in the woods near District 12 with her friend Gale and becomes very good at using a bow and arrow. When her younger sister, Prim, is picked as one of the tributes, Katniss decides to go in her place. The other tribute from District 12 is a boy named Peeta, and Katniss soon has a complicated relationship with him.

Writing about your dreams will help you remember more details, so think about the people and places in the dream because they might be important too. After a week, you will be surprised by how much you have written. Now you can link your dreams to what happens and how you feel in your daily life.

In the past, many bridges were built from wood and were very easy to catch fire. This was especially true for old train bridges, where sparks from the steel wheels and tracks could sometimes set the bridge on fire and make it burn down.

We cannot predict how street art will change in the future, but we can see some trends. Most street artists are young and paint in their local areas, but many are now traveling and working worldwide. Some artists use the internet to communicate and share pictures of their art. Additionally, the art world is starting to recognize street art as a real art form. Even though we don't know what will happen next, we can be sure that street art is not going away!

Suzanne Collines has always felt sad when watching news about wars. When she was a child, her father was a pilot in the US Air Force and fought in Vietnam. Her mother tried to keep her safe by not telling her about the war, but she still saw news about it and knew her dad was there. It was very scary for her.

A global survey by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) gathered responses from over 40,000 millennials (born between 1983 and 1993) and non-millennials about workplace culture, communication, pay, career growth, and work-life balance. Another global survey by Deloitte included over 10,000 millennials who shared their views on the challenges and opportunities in today's work environment.

Erik Weihenmayer from the United States is an adventurer. He has ridden a bike in the deserts of Morocco, kayaked in the Grand Canyon, and climbed Mount Everest. Remarkably, Erik has been blind since he was 13 years old. Besides his travels, he helps people with disabilities to be active and takes groups of young blind people climbing.

Online platforms are giving people a chance to make some extra money. For example, busy parents used to avoid selling their children's old things at local markets, but now they can easily sell barely used baby clothes and expensive baby gear online to earn some cash.

Pi and Richard Parker stay in the lifeboat for 227 days. They face hunger, sickness, and tiredness. They go through strong storms and the hot sun of the Pacific, but they manage to survive. Sometimes, Pi feels comfort from his three religions, but other times he feels very lonely and sad. At last, they see the Mexican coast, and everything changes. I won’t tell you the ending, so you need to read the book to see what happens to Pi and Richard Parker when they see land.

Chloe came home from school, made a cup of coffee, and took it to her bedroom. She had homework, but it could wait. She wanted to enjoy the quiet time before her parents came home and the house got noisy with talking, the TV, or her dad playing jazz while cooking. She liked this time because she could play with her pet rats.

In 2010, NASA's planetary defense team found and recorded 90 percent of the asteroids near Earth that are 1 kilometer wide. These 'near-Earth objects' (NEOs) are as big as mountains and include anything within 50 million kilometers of Earth's orbit. NASA estimates there are about 50 left to record, and says that none of the 887 known NEOs pose a serious threat to the planet.

Auggie decides to go to school, but his first day is very hard because he feels anxious and different. Other kids don't want to sit with him and often stare or whisper about him. Luckily, he makes friends with Jack and Summer. However, Auggie finds out that some classmates are afraid to touch him. Throughout the school year, he experiences many highs and lows until a surprising and difficult event at a school camp changes everything.

The two men looked at the northern part of the land, which seemed to go on forever. They could hardly see the fences from where they were. No matter how bored a teenage boy might feel, he couldn't escape by walking. Sam watched the biggest horse, which was kicking the ground with its strong hooves. He wondered if the boy could ride. A good rider could find a lot of trouble out here, far from anyone. But someone who didn't know about horses and wanted to leave his father might get into even more trouble.

More than 4,000 climbers, aged thirteen to eighty, have reached the top of Everest. Climbing high mountains in cold weather and strong storms is still very dangerous, but the best climbers in the world are now looking for new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria started to love mountain climbing when she was a teenager. After finishing school, she worked as a nurse but continued to climb in her free time.

After climbing Everest, Gerlinde chose to climb all fourteen of the world's mountains that are 8,000 meters high. To make it harder, she climbs without oxygen tanks, which is dangerous because low oxygen at high altitudes can harm the brain and body. Gerlinde also uses her fame as a climber to help a charity for poor children and orphans in Nepal.

If we look at the things we have bought in our lives, we can see that not everything is used well: the warm coat we thought was stylish even though we live in a hot country, the smartphone we stopped using when we got a new one, the car we only drive on weekends, or the guest room that has become a storage room.

Throughout history and in different cultures, dreams have been linked to predictions. People believed that dreams were messages from the gods, meant to give us knowledge or understanding. Even now, many people remember a time when they dreamed about something, and later that dream happened in real life.

Many large and costly transportation projects around the world include building bridges. Bridges are important connections that allow cars, trucks, and trains to cross water, deep valleys, or other roads. Therefore, they are a key part of civil engineering and are closely examined, especially when they fall down.

After weeks of feeling frustrated, Gabriela emailed her Swedish manager about the problems she was having with her team. Her manager just asked if she thought her team was still doing well and what could help her work better with them. Gabriela thought her manager was unclear and didn't feel he was handling the situation well.

Dogs that live in groups have learned that humans often give food to smaller, cuter dogs, so those dogs go to ask for food for everyone. Some dogs can even use the city's metro to move around their area! Scientists are not sure how the dogs know when to get off the train. One idea is that they use their strong sense of smell to recognize the scents of places they like. Another idea is that they understand the names of stations from announcements. Either way, people on the metro have become so used to seeing dogs on the trains that they hardly notice them.

Ed Stafford from the UK was the first person to walk the whole length of the Amazon River. He began at a small stream in the Andes mountains of Peru and reached the river's end in Brazil after two years and four months, walking 6,000 kilometers. The Amazon rainforest has dangerous animals like poisonous snakes, crocodiles, and jaguars, so Ed was always at risk. Fortunately, he only got a few thousand bites from mosquitoes and ants.

In Britain, the average person spends over £1,000 on new clothes each year, which is about four percent of their income. This may not seem like a lot, but it shows two bigger problems for society and the environment. First, many people are using credit cards to pay for these clothes. British adults owe about £670 each to credit card companies, which is 66 percent of what they spend on clothes. Also, people are spending money they don't have to buy things they don't need. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothing every year, most of which ends up in landfills.

Ed's walk would not have been possible without technology. He used a radio to ask the rainforest people for food and permission to cross their land. Many of them came to meet him and helped him through the hardest parts of the journey. As he walked, Ed wrote a blog about his daily experiences. He used the media attention from his trip to speak out against the destruction of the rainforest and to raise money for environmental and children's charities in Brazil and Peru.

Businesses have realized that they can make money from the sharing economy by using resources that are not fully used. A popular business model now is where companies create online platforms to connect customers with people who offer specific products or services. For example, Airbnb helps people rent out their empty rooms and houses for extra income. Another example is Uber, which allows people to use their own cars as taxis to earn extra money in their spare time.

One important job of modern zoos is to help breed endangered animals from different countries. In nature, some rare animals struggle to find partners and have babies, and they face dangers from hunters, losing their homes, and other animals that might attack them. A good zoo allows these animals to live and reproduce safely. Also, as some wild animal numbers decrease, there is a risk that they will become too similar genetically. Breeding programs help by allowing zoo-bred animals to be released into the wild, which increases genetic diversity.

Both types of accidents are very rare, but boats and trains can cause a bridge to fall for different reasons. Trains can bring down a bridge because of their speed, while boats can do it because they are very heavy, even if they are moving slowly. To prevent bridge failures, it is important to plan ahead. New technologies that find weak spots, safer work areas, and better designs can help reduce these serious accidents.

At first, Pi is scared of the animals and jumps into the ocean. Then he remembers there are hungry sharks in the water and knows he must climb back into the lifeboat. One by one, the animals in the lifeboat kill and eat each other, until only Pi and the tiger are left. Luckily for Pi, the tiger, whom he names Richard Parker, feels sick and does not want to eat him right away.

When Pi is 16, a new government is elected that his parents do not like. Worried about what will happen next, Pi's parents decide to close the zoo and move to Canada. Some animals are sold to zoos in North America, and the family travels by ship to Canada with the animals. During the journey, a big storm happens and the ship sinks. Sadly, Pi's family and the sailors drown, but Pi ends up in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orangutan, and a large tiger.

The Hunger Games is a very popular book for teens and young adults written by American author Suzanne Collins. Since it came out in 2008, it has been translated into 26 languages and has sold millions of copies worldwide. It was also the first book for young readers to sell over a million e-books. The Hunger Games is now a big Hollywood movie and is just as successful, making 152.5 million dollars in its first weekend in North America!

Dreams might happen because our mind is sorting out our daily thoughts, but they show up in dreams with special meanings. When we are awake, we usually think in words, like talking to ourselves. But when we sleep, the part of our brain for language is less active, while the part for emotions is more active.

Having good relationships is very important for happiness. A study showed that happy people usually have strong connections with friends and family and spend time with them often. You also need at least one person to share your personal feelings with, which is called 'self-disclosure'. Just one close friend is enough, along with other relationships. It's not enough to have many friends just to hang out or talk about music or football; that deeper connection matters a lot. Some people need to learn how to listen better to build stronger relationships.

Psychologist Carol Dweck talked about how our brains can change and how we can learn new skills, even if we weren't good at them before. Many people often praise the final results and natural talents, like saying, "You are great at noticing details" or "You are really good at planning events." However, studies show that if we focus on how things are done—like praising hard work, trying new things, and solving problems—we can help people learn new skills and improve their talents.

The rover checks the air around it from time to time, and in 2014 it discovered that the air had methane, which is a simple organic molecule and an important part of natural gas. Methane only lasts a few hundred years, so something on Mars must be making more of it. NASA says Mars releases thousands of tons of methane at once, and the amount of methane goes up and down with the seasons, like the planet is breathing.

At the start of her career, psychologist Carol Dweck from Stanford University gave ten-year-olds some problems that were a bit too difficult. One group liked the challenge and believed they could improve their skills. She called this a 'growth mindset' because they focused on what they could achieve later. However, another group felt judged and thought they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and couldn't see how they could get better. Some of these children said they might cheat later, while others looked for someone who did worse than them to feel better about themselves.

Horror films often take place in empty locations like abandoned hospitals, scary houses, or ghost towns. These lonely places make us wonder what life was like when people were there and why they left. Their silence can be very frightening too. Plus, these places are useful for horror film directors because there is usually no phone signal there.

Basements are scary places in horror films, no matter what type of house it is. They are often dark and damp, and you can only get to them by a narrow staircase. Something is usually hiding there, or the bad person has hidden their tools. Basements always feel creepy, even if there is nothing there.

Gary Collins, a policeman on holiday, saw the London riots on TV and recognized some people. He cut his holiday short to help identify them. He spent six months looking at CCTV footage and identified 190 people, often just by their eyes. His help was very important for the investigation. Even with 200,000 hours of video, facial recognition software only identified one person.

I find it interesting to think about how we can make our evolution faster by improving our bodies. Imagine if we could put a computer in our brain! Soon, we will be able to do this and improve our math skills, how we see and hear, and our memory. This idea will become more common.

The talk was very interesting, and the speaker made some good points. For example, how can we expect teenagers not to text while doing homework when they see their parents using social media while cooking or waiting at a red light? She also mentioned that people want to be in many places at once, so they switch between real-life and online conversations. I notice this with my teenage daughter and her friends; they meet up but often sit quietly while talking to others online.

While news stories often make us think the world is more violent, there is some good news too. From the end of World War II to 1990, there were 30 wars that killed over 100,000 people. Today, there are still civil wars, but countries are generally living together more peacefully than before. However, terrorism has increased in recent years, and since World War II, more civilians have died in wars than soldiers. Still, the statistics for civilians are not all bad. Although violent crime is nine times more likely to cause deaths than political conflict, the global murder rate has slightly decreased, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

Wasfia has spent her life helping human rights and has seen many projects in her country that teach women and girls, but often these projects end and leave them with nothing. She realized that Bangladesh needed to be strong, so she combined her love for climbing and human rights to change how people view women in her country. She started climbing while working on humanitarian projects in Tibet and Nepal because most people in flat Bangladesh have never seen a mountain. Her campaign is working, as people in her country and around the world are starting to pay attention.

Many people think that developing countries are very poor, ruled by dictators, and have no hope for change. However, this is not true. In fact, a big change is happening. In the last 20 years, over 700 million people have earned more money and escaped poverty. Also, six million fewer children die from sickness each year, more girls are going to school, and many more people have clean water.

Many managers try to make their feedback more positive by placing negative comments between two positive ones. However, if this becomes a habit, employees may see positive comments as just a way to soften the negatives, which makes them less valuable. Positive feedback should not just be used to soften the negative but should be given to support and encourage good work.

I am part of the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Instead of thinking about scary robots from movies, consider what is happening now: military machines like drones and robots are already being used to kill with little human control. The next step will be robots that can decide who to kill by themselves. I believe this is very wrong and could be dangerous for people. We must be very careful about what we let machines do.

More people are learning English than all other languages together, and English is spoken in the most countries. However, Chinese has the most native speakers. There is not much connection between the number of native speakers and learners, but there is a stronger connection between the number of learners and the number of countries where the language is spoken.

Your manager stops you and says she wants to talk about how you did on the recent project. You worry about it all weekend, thinking about what you might have done wrong. When you go into her office on Monday morning, she starts by complimenting your good work on the project, and you think this might be the usual nice-then-critique-then-nice feedback style. You know how it works: say something nice, give the real feedback, then say something nice again.

Born in the USA is a lively rock album with catchy songs, but its lyrics are deep and emotional. The songs tell stories about the struggles of everyday people who feel angry and disappointed because life hasn't given them wealth or fame. For example, the song Glory Days is about small-town people remembering their youth, while Downbound Train tells the story of a young man whose life falls apart after losing his job. It seems the artist is inspired by real people he knew and the life he could have had if he hadn't become famous. The album clearly shows the amazing talent of the Boss.

Lewis wants the number of marine protected areas in the world to grow from 3 percent to 10 percent to help fix the harm done by human activities like overfishing, pollution, and littering. He has seen this damage himself during his trips. He has swum over coral reefs that have lost their color because of warmer water and has seen lifeless areas in the Red Sea filled with plastic. Pugh thinks that nature can heal if we give it a chance, but time is running out. If we don't take care of our oceans, we might face a big problem soon.

Terrie Sharp, a best-selling author who has won the Olive Crime Writer Award twice, knows how to tell great stories. She grew up in a tough area of Glasgow and learned to stay safe and open car doors with a knife. Fortunately, she only uses these skills for her writing now and is often seen on popular daytime shows like Police Today and at writing conferences across the UK.

Are things getting worse every day? Is it impossible to make progress? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker examines human progress and finds positive news. We are living longer, healthier, freer, and happier lives. Pinker believes the real issue is that the values of reason and science from the Enlightenment are being challenged. When commentators and leaders play on people's tribalism, hopelessness, and distrust, we risk harming important institutions like democracy and global cooperation.

In old horror movies, when the main characters were in trouble, they often couldn't call for help or the police. Now, with mobile phones, that seems less real.
