To keep the suspense, there is no phone signal! If you are a hero in a horror movie, it is very likely that when you really need to call for help, you won't have any signal. Or your phone battery will die right when you try to call. Or both.

In the 1950s, banana farmers in Central America were losing their most profitable banana, the Gros Michel, also called Big Mike. Now, the same thing is happening to its replacement, the Cavendish. The Gros Michel banana was popular because it was easy to transport, had thick skin, and tasted sweet. United Fruit, the biggest banana grower and exporter in South America at that time, produced bananas very efficiently by cloning shoots from the plants instead of using seeds and growing them in crowded fields.

Most spiders have venom that helps them catch their food, not to hurt people. Only 25 types of spiders can harm humans, and while their bites can hurt, they usually aren't deadly. The Sydney funnel-web spider in Australia hasn't caused any deaths since the anti-venom was made in 1981. However, be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas. If they feel threatened, they can release irritating hairs that can get stuck in your skin or eyes.

This common idea in horror films was very popular in the late 20th century. It begins with a group of teenagers having fun, and it ends with everyone dead except one girl. At first, the girl is usually innocent, shy, and not very strong. By the end, she becomes the strongest and smartest person. The last girl almost always wins.

To understand where our ability to use complex language comes from, we need to examine how our brains are different from those of other animals. This is not just about brain size; it also matters what other functions our brains have and how and why they developed over time. There are very few physical clues to help us; the tools left by our ancestors do not show us what kind of speech they could produce. However, we can see changes in the mouth, throat, and tongue of early humans. By around 100,000 years ago, humans could make complex sounds. Before that, scientists can only guess if early humans communicated with simpler sounds.

Society, not nature, tells us that girls should prefer arts and humanities while boys take maths and physics. There are not enough positive female role models in science for young people to see. Cartoons and stories often show scientists, inventors, and astronauts as men. Also, there is a wrong idea that scientists are nerdy, have bad social skills, or work alone. These stereotypes from the media can make girls feel like they don’t belong in science and see it as an unattractive career. If girls had more positive female role models in science, it would help them feel more confident and included in those subjects.

The Scallion is a free weekly newspaper made by students and given out in faculty buildings, read by about 10,000 students. A survey shows that university students and staff appreciate it for entertainment, culture, and work experience. Printing the newspaper costs a lot. Some students find it hard to get a copy because they must go to the university to pick it up. Also, many copies become litter on campus, which is bad for the environment.

At Girox Foods, about 12 out of every 100 employees leave each year. This number seems high because the usual rate in the industry is 7 out of 100. This report aims to find out why employees feel engaged at work and to suggest ways to make their experience better and keep them from leaving.

Much of what the speaker said was true. I believe that being more connected can make us feel more alone. My generation, who grew up without technology, knows how to be alone and that it's okay. But for those under 20, it's different. They are always communicating and may not learn to enjoy being alone. Also, they are learning to talk through messages that can be changed, instead of having real conversations with people face to face.

Don't always give negative feedback after positive feedback. If you always mix them, people might not value the positive comments. Make sure to give positive feedback sometimes without adding criticism.
